A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe EcoDiff and retain identifiable methods, experiments, and illustrations. The text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original pruning benchmarks in Table 2, checkpointing measurements in Figure 7, and additional SD2, retraining, and ablation results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original pruning comparisons in Table 1, post-pruning recovery results in Table 2, and a LAION retraining study in Appendix F, alongside retained experiments.

M1.justification: v1 explicitly uses an L1 penalty on mask parameters; v2 specifies the hard-concrete expected L0 penalty instead, changing the stated optimization objective (v1 Section 4.3; v2 Section 5.3). v2 also adds optional full-model fine-tuning alongside the LoRA recovery already present in v1 Appendix F. The masking locations, final-latent matching, and checkpointing procedure remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix F.2 adds retraining on real images from a LAION2B-en-aesthetic subset, extending the earlier synthetic GCC3M-prompt recovery data. GCC3M calibration and MS COCO/Flickr30K evaluation remain. The explicit flow-model terminology and additional FLUX configuration do not introduce a new generation task.

E2.justification: The main comparison changes from DiffPruning and DeepCache in v1 Table 2 to DiffPruning, BK-SDM, and per-step-loss masking for SDXL, with FLUX-Lite additionally evaluated for FLUX-Dev in v2 Table 1. DeepCache remains in the compatibility appendix but is removed as a main-table comparator.

E3.justification: v1's main comparison explicitly excludes retraining and reports SDXL at 10/20% and FLUX-Schnell at 10/15% pruning. v2 specifies a shared 10-A100-hour/100-sample budget, except for FLUX-Lite, emphasizes 20% pruning, and adds FLUX-Dev pruning and expanded recovery protocols. Speedup replaces GFLOPs in the main table. Its new 50-step mask-learning description is unreconciled with the retained 400-step configuration tables; these reported revisions do not establish controlled cross-version reruns.

E4.justification: v2 adds a direct end-to-end versus per-step-loss comparison, expands the earlier 25/30% LoRA recovery study to LoRA versus full-model recovery across 25–50% sparsity, and tests synthetic versus LAION retraining data. It removes the hard-discrete sampling illustrations and delta analysis. Existing regularization, calibration-size, module-selection, thresholding, and checkpointing analyses are largely retained or relocated.

E5.justification: Five-run averaging for checkpointing measurements is unchanged (v1 Figure 7; v2 Figure 15). However, v2 removes the sampling illustrations and their single-, 10-, and 100-run information from v1 Figure 4 and Appendix C. No new uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced for the benchmark scores.

E6.justification: The main SDXL 20%-pruned MS COCO/Flickr FIDs change from 34.41/42.84 to 32.19/40.91, while unpruned FIDs change from 35.50/49.34 to 27.43/33.95 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 1). Thus, the within-version FID ranking against the original model reverses. Differently reported protocols prevent interpreting this as a controlled performance gain. v2 also adds FLUX-Dev comparisons, speedup entries, and extensive high-sparsity recovery and LAION results.

T1.justification: Appendix A replaces v1's approximation of the sparsity penalty by an L1 norm with a logistic-probability derivation of the expected active-gate count under delta approaching zero. This revises the mathematical justification and corrects the use of the location and temperature parameters. v2 also introduces an explicit flow-sampling Euler update and formalizes the per-step loss; the checkpointing asymptotic claims remain.

C1.justification: The central claim shifts from pruning without retraining and without performance loss to achieving 20% sparsity within a small stated compute/calibration budget and without extensive retraining. The abstract and introduction explicitly position EcoDiff for diffusion and flow models, while lightweight LoRA and full-model recovery become stated contributions rather than an appendix-only compatibility result.

C2.justification: v2 adds arguments about unequal step importance and assumed-correct intermediate inputs when explaining per-step loss failures. It attributes low SSIM to acceptable texture/detail shifts and discusses LoRA's limited recovery at high sparsity versus full-model adaptation. Appendix F additionally interprets the LAION results as evidence that recovery is not solely an artifact of synthetic retraining data. These substantially extend v1's interpretations and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 adds detailed LoRA and full-model retraining configurations, including rank, batch size, learning rates, resolutions, and 100 versus 10,000 synthetic prompts; v1 only summarized the LoRA data and training duration. It changes reported hardware from H100 to A100, corrects the SDXL checkpoint entry, clarifies hard-concrete parameters, and adds a reproducibility statement with an embedded repository link. These are documented disclosures, not verification of external resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around classical learned-mask pruning and diffusion-training efficiency. It adds discussion of BK-SDM, FLUX-Lite, EPTI, LoRA, Sheared LLaMA, and other relevant work, including acknowledgment of prior unstructured pruning with limited retraining. This changes the novelty context beyond citation-format or bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper, substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, and results narrative, adds a standalone per-step-loss discussion, and moves the pruning objective before the masking description. Post-pruning adaptation becomes part of the main narrative, several analyses move to appendices, and ethics and reproducibility statements replace the earlier ending structure with its dedicated limitations section.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column presentation and rebuilds the main comparison table with speedup and compute-budget columns. It revises qualitative comparison grids and adds full-model recovery displays. Neuron-masking, pruning-ratio, and checkpointing figures move to appendices; the hard-discrete plots and additional baseline gallery are removed. These are substantial display and layout changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's L1 approximation and limited LoRA recovery study, v2 strengthens the mathematical explanation, directly tests the per-step-loss alternative, and documents broader recovery experiments. However, the 50-versus-400-step descriptions remain unreconciled, and identical FLUX-Schnell scores appear at 20% pruning in Table 1 and 15% in Table 6. The prose also retains an SDXL FID-improvement interpretation contradicted by the revised main table. These reporting problems limit the net quality gain.
